source.title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
source.authors: Dashiell Stander; Qi-Nan Yu; Honglu Fan; Stella Biderman

record.tranche_reason: It reports grokking on a different small algorithmic task, permutation-group multiplication, and analyzes the mechanism using coset concentration and causal interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly says its S5 and S6 models grokked and reached perfect test accuracy, but it trains only with a 40% training set and does not compare training-set sizes. Its temporal circuit measurements bear on gradual circuit formation, but it does not test whether memorizing components are removed later or whether progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump. The causal interventions in Table 1 test properties of the proposed coset circuit, not the timing of grokking, so they are not included as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The paper trains MLPs that grok S5/S6 multiplication at a 40% train split. It tracks coset-circuit formation during training and compares circuits across seeds. These results bear on V1, V2 and V6. The work is mainly interpretability, and grokking itself is reported in words only, with no accuracy curves.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that one-hidden-layer MLPs that grokked S5/S6 multiplication implement it with coset circuits built on subgroup structure, with subgroup mixtures varying across seeds. They argue that the GCR algorithm of Chughtai et al. for the same setup does not explain the evidence. Their main takeaway is that proposed mechanisms must be validated with causal interventions, not observational evidence alone.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses one-hidden-layer fully connected networks for permutation-group multiplication in S5 and S6, rather than the original modular-arithmetic task; it trains with a 40% training set.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that different runs form coset circuits at different times and use varying subgroup mixtures; S5 and S6 also use different widths, embedding sizes, and training durations.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating neurons with coset concentration ≥1 leaves accuracy unchanged in 126/128 S5 models; the other two drop to 99% and 98%. Causal interventions (Table 1) confirm the properties of the coset circuit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In grokked group-multiplication MLPs, the final generalizing computation is carried almost entirely by coset-concentrated neurons.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: For the grokking claim, the paper reports only one training-set fraction and does not provide numerical chance-level test accuracy or a quantitative delay comparison across data sizes. The temporal circuit evidence includes figure-based trajectories and a single-neuron example; the paper does not establish that circuit progress anticipates the test-accuracy jump.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 causal interventions (embedding exchange, sign changes, noise perturbations, and replacing ReLU with absolute value) were omitted because they test circuit properties rather than the grokking timing or claim versions recorded here. Figure 5 thresholds beyond the reported threshold minH∈Sub(G) CH(Ni) ≥ 1 were omitted because they are not needed for the claim rows.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size: only a 40% split is used. No quantitative delay or chance-level accuracy is reported.
Whether memorizing components are removed later, and whether a progress measure precedes the test-accuracy jump.
Entire version: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Entire version: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Entire version: weight decay is fixed at 1.0 and is not varied. No critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
Variation across architecture and hyperparameters; only random seeds vary.
Entire version: Adam is used throughout with no optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: Over 99.2% of linear-layer neurons across all 128 S5 and 100 S6 runs have min C_H < 1, mostly below 1e-6. Every run converges on coset neurons, the cross-run commonality bearing on V6.
Other neuron-formation trajectories: an S3×S2 neuron forming over 140k–160k steps and an A4 neuron over 100k–250k steps. Further evidence of gradual circuit formation.
Statement that different runs form coset circuits at different times in training.
The same subgroup (e.g. D10) forms coset circuits concentrated on different irreps in different runs while behaving identically. This bears on whether runs share an identifiable algorithm.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T2 is kept: the paper uses a mechanistic, mainly interpretability method on a near-original algorithmic setting (Power et al. included S5). Grokking evidence (V1) is asserted, not plotted. The ablation rows (r6, r7) were relinked to 'none' because they bear on the final circuit, not on grokking dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare different training-set sizes or measure how the delay changes as the training set shrinks.

It measures the development of coset circuits over training, but does not show memorizing components being removed later or establish that a continuous progress measure anticipates the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
Weight decay is used, but its efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking prediction are not tested.
The paper compares runs with different seeds, but does not vary architecture or hyperparameters.
The paper uses Adam but does not test optimizer or numerical-artifact explanations.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer fully connected model trained on S5 (aggregate of 128 runs)
rows.operation_detail: Train on S5 group multiplication; the paper reports the models exhibit grokking.
rows.measure: Training-to-test generalization and final test accuracy
rows.value: The models are described as first memorizing the training set and much later generalizing; the analyzed models have perfect test accuracy.
rows.note: The paper does not give a numerical chance-level test accuracy or a per-run delay for this aggregate.
rows.check: Grokking is a text assertion only. No train/test accuracy curves, chance level or delay length are reported. Power et al. also used S5 composition, so S5 is not wholly a new task.

rows.subject: S5 model, seed 1
